Tykocin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tykocin, Poland

Not demolished. Tykocin's Jews, present from the start of the 16th century, formed one of the most important religious communities in the First Polish Republic; the town's population was 49 percent Jewish by 1921, most shot by the Germans on August 25–26, 1941, in nearby Łopuchów. This cemetery was established following a 1522 privilege granted by Olbracht Gasztołd. During WWII, the Germans executed both Jews and Poles at the cemetery; on September 10, 1943, Władysława Krysiewicz was shot dead there for helping Jews. Destruction continued after the war as some Poles used matzevot for farm purposes; the site later served as a marketplace under Communist rule.
